rules.rule: Claude must work from the expected canonical HEAD of config-par-environnement; stale-main derived execution is blocked before coding.
Autonomous code/test/fix loops are allowed in NEXUS Test within the approved lot; Production access is not implied.

An optional Test capability that is unavailable must degrade explicitly instead of preventing Claude from starting; any proof that actually requires that capability remains unsatisfied and fail-closed.
service_role is allowed only behind a trusted server or NEXUS Connector and is forbidden in repository, browser and public workflow logs.
The creator administers NEXUS but the client company controls use and sharing of its data; company/site context must be explicit and isolated.

No application or Production change to main, production, Supabase Production or NEXUS Production without Frederic's explicit approval; the only main exception is the human-authorized orchestration control-plane defined by ADR-0003.

A main-branch workflow change is allowed only for the orchestration control-plane, with Frederic's explicit authorization, no application files, no Production access expansion and no cleartext secret.
A business truth has one logical owner; wrappers, CIN and UI consume it and do not rebuild a parallel calculation.

When the SCOPE of a rule changes, change it at every read that guards a write, not only where the symptom appeared. Enumerate the reads first, fix them in one pass, then assert the old scope is absent everywhere. A scope left behind is silent by nature: the guard finds a row that belongs to another scope, concludes the work is already done, and skips the write while reporting success.
rules.source: 2026-09-13: the scope « already pointed » moved from (employee, date, type) to (employee, service, type). It was fixed in five places in the morning and a sixth was found that evening — the read guarding the pause-close written at departure time. Two services on one day, and the departure was recorded alone while the second break stayed open forever, with no message. Each fix had targeted where someone had stumbled, never the rule.

rules.rule: Claude fixes and retests failures inside the authorized lot without opening a new decision cycle; escalate only when the fix changes scope or doctrine.
Never wake Claude twice for the same canonical decision while the first wake is active, successful, or its outcome is unknown; verify issue #28, workflow state and canonical Handoff first.

If the first Claude wake for a canonical decision has objectively ended unsuccessfully and the decision remains unconsumed, no request return exists, and no equivalent Claude run is active, Orchestrator may issue exactly one controlled retry for the same decision. A second failed retry must not loop; record the incident and escalate the rail failure to Orchestrator for diagnosis before any further wake.
After each lot, promote durable knowledge to rules/ADR/Bible and recurring incidents to automatic checks so a twice-solved problem does not require a third identical human analysis.
Maximum truck volume is an optimization target, never an obligation; complement only when physically safe and absorbable by forecast rotation without inventing future sales.

A detector must be calibrated against the real repository before being wired into CI, and its finding count reported before and after. A guard that emits dozens of false positives is disabled within a week, taking with it the real findings it would have caught later. Noise is a failure mode, not an inconvenience.

A mutation must be proven to have actually modified the source before its result is read, and a hypothesis must be measured before it is acted upon. A sed that matches nothing returns a meaningless 'survived'; an unmeasured hypothesis sends the fix to the wrong place.
rules.source: 3 silent seds on 2026-09-07; pilesParPosition hypothesis measured at 0.0% of profile

rules.rule: An assertion must be able to fail. Anchor patterns or quote the expected phrase; capture every stream the program under test writes to; never let a catch swallow the signal. Mechanised by outils/guardian-qa.js.
rules.source: /2/ matching issue-28, /OK/ unanchored, stdout-only helper on stderr output

rules.rule: Work is not delivered because it exists on a branch. A cloud run pushes a branch and nothing merges it: the silence looks exactly like success. Every work branch must end either merged into the canonical branch or recorded in docs/handoff/BRANCHES-CLASSEES.json with a sort, a motive and the exact sha covered. Mechanised by outils/garde-branches-en-rade.js and surfaced in NEXUS Live.
rules.source: three branches carrying an already-rendered arbitration waited unnoticed on 2026-09-08; the Live MVP and the CARB-004 fix had the same fate earlier

rules.rule: A local bench must share its assumptions with the real environment, and be runnable before pushing. A scenario calibrated against one station's configuration and seeded into another is proven locally and false in reality. Snapshot the real configuration, calibrate against that snapshot, and let CI verify the snapshot has not drifted. Mechanised by outils/repetition-recette-carburants.js. The same applies to shell: reproduce the runner exact flags. GitHub `shell: bash` runs with `-e`, which `set -uo pipefail` does not disable — a bare `var=$(cmd)` whose command fails kills the step before any message, making the very branches written to name that failure unreachable. Test with `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`.
rules.source: 2026-09-08: four commits and four six-minute CI cycles to make one seed work, because CI was the only place the real environment could be exercised and it reveals one obstacle at a time; the scenario itself had been calibrated with another station tanks; and 2026-09-08: four CI-visible cases proven locally with plain `bash script` passed, then died silently in CI under -e; and 2026-09-08 again: the fuel scenario was validated across seven weekdays but a SINGLE hour, and broke at 13:25 when the 11:00 order cutoff lengthened the sales window — seven days at one hour was half the domain

rules.rule: When a permission blocks an automated step, find the exact mechanism by EXPERIMENT before choosing a fix, then prefer the fix that PRESERVES least privilege over the convenient one. Widening a read or write capability to satisfy a SQL convenience is a permanent cost paid for a temporary comfort; reshaping the statement is usually free.
rules.source: 2026-09-08: publishing the NEXUS Live journal was refused under RLS. Four hypotheses failed in a row — the table grant, the write policy, the emitted actor roles, then a conflict with an invisible row — before an experiment showed the `ON CONFLICT` clause itself requires a read POLICY under RLS, which a table grant does not provide. Granting the CI role read access to the Creator execution journal would have worked; publishing row by row without `ON CONFLICT`, and treating a duplicate key as the expected fact it is, kept the role write-only and needed no new privilege.

rules.rule: A test must never require a known defect to be PRESENT. Asserting that the repository still contains the bug locks it in: the day it is fixed, that test breaks and CI reports the fix as a regression. Prove the detector with synthetic fixtures; use the real repository to check the defect does not COME BACK.
rules.source: 2026-09-08: closing CARB-007 removed the copied truck capacity from a screen, and test_guardian_regles_metier failed with « la capacité camion recopiée hors du moteur doit rester visible » — the fix was flagged as a new failing test

rules.rule: A declared wake_to is a logical role (ChatGPT, Claude), not necessarily a postable channel. Before treating a blocked next action as requiring a human STOP, resolve the role to a concrete, reachable address through a committed fact (never a hard-coded destination in tooling); only when no resolution exists is the stoppage BLOCKED_TECHNIQUE rather than CHANNEL_LIMITATION. A closed-list STOP motive always wins over a resolved channel.
rules.source: 2026-10-07: GOUVERNANCE-REFERENCE-CODE-20261005/request-6.md declared wake_to: ChatGPT with green local CI; tests.yml's publication step only accepts a literal <server>/<repo>/issues/<n> address, so the wake stayed confined to the run summary and the chain stalled despite an available channel — fixed by docs/handoff/CANAUX.json + outils/reveil-orchestrateur.js::resoudreCanal, mechanised by outils/classification-canal.js

rules.rule: A condition an arbiter retained as the basis of a favourable verdict is not a control until code enforces it. Before declaring a preparation compliant with the arbiter's conditions, locate each retained condition in executable code; a condition that exists only in the request's prose, in the decision's prose or in a comment must be reported as ABSENT, never counted as held. The same applies to a substitute control a decision claims to have performed by hand: if nothing re-performs it, the next deposit is unprotected.
rules.source: 2026-10-10: ARMEMENT-ARBITRAGE-AUTONOME-1-20261008/request-1.md announced five refusals for stade (a) and decision-1.md retained them as conditions of its APPROVED (SHA comparison, no automatic consumption, fast-forward only); stade (a) was then armed and materialised three decisions on the rail while outils/materialiser-decision-ci.js enforced none of RAIL_LU, the SHA comparison or the human tier — fixed by lectureDuRail/relaieUnHumain plus exit code 4 and its CI wiring, proven by mutation (M12-M20, X2, X3)

rules.rule: Calibrate a guard on the artefacts the repository really holds, on the field's real POSITION and not the one its documentation implies, before wiring it. Read the two or three authentic files, print what the guard reads from them, and lock that measurement into an epreuve so the guard dies if it stops measuring the real form. A guard that refuses every genuine artefact gets disarmed within the week, and takes with it the true findings it would have made later.
rules.source: 2026-10-10: the RAIL_LU guard was first written to read the field from the parsed NEXT_ACTION_CONTRACT block; both authentic decisions of ARMEMENT-ARBITRAGE-AUTONOME-1-20261008 write RAIL_LU BEFORE that line (decision-1.md:70 vs :73, decision-2.md:38 vs :40), where lireContrat never reaches it, so the guard would have refused every real verdict — found by grep before committing, fixed by lireRailLu over the whole text, calibration locked into epreuve M17

rules.rule: In a patch or migration script, a global string replace also rewrites longer identifiers that contain the anchor and the author's own deliberately-written call sites. Assert the expected occurrence count for every anchor before replacing, and refuse the patch when the count differs; a protective no-op replace of the longer form protects nothing. Prefer a raw-string Python patch to a shell heredoc when the target contains JS template literals, where backticks and ${} are inert.
rules.source: 2026-10-10: while extending test_materialiser_decision_ci_20261009.js, replacing 'm.juger(' with 'jg(' also rewrote the inside of 'mm.juger(' into 'mjg(' (3 call sites broken) and rewrote epreuve M15's deliberately unwrapped m.juger call, which then silently received default SHAs and reported a passing fail-closed test as 0 instead of 2; found by running the harness (17/21), fixed with per-anchor occurrence assertions
